comment_data.body:
Wondering if it being just a constant 2 is fine or if it would make more sense to wait longer and longer before retrying, capping it at some ceiling? For example: 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 64... resetting it so that the sequence starts anew when appropriate, e.g. when a direct connection gets lost and we need to start trying to establish it again.

Does this also affect hole-punching to the gc peer?

comment_data.body:
Yes, I admit, this is more of a band-aid. Something like exponential backoff like you are proposing would be better. But I tried to keep it simple and this is a very significant reduction, reducing wasted traffic by multiple orders of magnitude for my use case.

> Does this also affect hole-punching to the gc peer?

I do not actually know how this works, @JFreegman can you comment on that?

comment_data.body:
Yeah, I'm not sure if the incremental backoff is the best solution, I just thought that if we are unable to establish a direct connection within some reasonable time, say 10 seconds, the likelihood of us establishing it soon after, until some network conditions change, is rather low and we shouldn't keep re-trying as often as possibly every 2 seconds, wasting data on sending duplicate messages. Phone plans still have data caps and slow-down speeds once the cap is reached, so being more conscious of sending too much data might be a good idea, or perhaps it could be a toxcore-wide Tox_Options flag -- to optimize the usage for mobile, as opposed to assuming you have a 1Gbps unlimited fiber internet connection.

Anyway, I will let @JFreegman decide what he thinks is the best here, he is the code expert of gc. Resolving this change request thread.

I definitely think there needs to be more leeway than this. UDP connections can be weird and take a bit of time to be established. What's the actual source of this bug, anyhow? Alice knows Bob's IP, Bob knows Alice's IP, but for whatever reason they can't establish a UDP connection?

Edit: And no I don't think it affects hole punching.

Yes.


> Edit: And no I don't think it affects hole punching.

Good to know.

Change of plans. I took a look and NGC simply has no NAT hole punching code, making this double sending act as such.

So we need to replace this with some proper code, either by copying the existing code from dht, or writing something new.

I will lower the timer to once per second and push this as a quick fix to get this into the release.
